columns.description: Whether the link is to a PROPERTY (`facility`) or only to the operating entity (`tribe`). A tribe-level row is a fact about the entity and is NOT attributable to any one of its properties - an online sportsbook is not a building and a compact authorises a tribe.
columns.name: entity_level

columns.description: Confidence tier of the ENTITY LINK, INHERITED verbatim from the facility row that carries it. It is never assigned by the table that holds it. An exact join on facility_id is exact; that says nothing about whether the facility itself was correctly keyed, and treating an exact key as strong evidence is the error that attributed a Wisconsin United Way to a California tribe at tier A.
columns.name: entity_tier

columns.description: Where entity_tier came from, in words, so a reader can see that it was inherited rather than assigned. Blank tier plus a stated basis means no tier could be inherited and none was invented.
columns.name: entity_tier_basis

columns.description: Which rung produced the link. `facility_id_exact` - the row names a facility that exists in the hub and carries an entity. `multi_property_host_unanimous_tribe` - a website host serving several properties that all belong to one tribe; linked at tribe level only, at the WEAKEST tier in the group. `row_tribe_id_mirror` - the row is tribe-level by design and this mirrors a link an earlier build made; it creates no new link. `ruled_nigc_name_exact` - an exact join into gaming_nigc_roster_link, a ruled table. `not_tribe_attributable_by_source` - the source states this licensee is not a Native entity; a correct answer, not a gap. NO RUNG USES A COORDINATE: proximity is weaker evidence than a name, and running it first let `Sportman's Bar` claim `4 Bears Casino & Lodge`.

columns.description: Whether this measurement type may promote to an ACTIVE headcount. `FORM5500_ACTIVE_PARTICIPANTS` is NEVER_PROMOTES_TO_ACTIVE because ACTIVE PARTICIPANTS ARE PEOPLE ENROLLED IN A BENEFIT PLAN, NOT EMPLOYEES: the count includes separated employees who still hold a balance and excludes employees who never enrolled or sit below the plan's age/service threshold. The two errors do not cancel and their net sign is not stable. It must never be relabelled as headcount. `OSHA_TRIBE_LEVEL_REPORTED` does promote - it is an employer-filed headcount.
columns.name: measurement_type_status

columns.description: Total hours worked by all employees at the establishment, as filed on the OSHA 300A. INCLUDES overtime and EXCLUDES paid leave, holidays and sick time.
columns.name: total_hours_worked

columns.description: DERIVED, NOT FILED: total_hours_worked / 2080. It travels in its own column and MUST NEVER enter `employment`, which holds the filed headcount. Two biases run in opposite directions and do not cancel - overtime is in the hours, so FTE is inflated above true full-time staffing; paid leave is not, so a salaried full-timer with three weeks off books ~1,960 hours and scores 0.94 FTE. Measured on these rows: median FTE/headcount 0.818 (p10-p90 0.594-1.000). The ratio is a staffing-mix measure, not an error.
columns.name: fte_2080

columns.description: 2080 = 40 hours x 52 weeks. A CONVENTION (the federal OPM/BLS FTE divisor), not a measurement of this employer's full-time year.
columns.name: fte_divisor

columns.description: Always 1. Present so no consumer can mistake fte_2080 for a filed figure.
columns.name: fte_is_derived_not_filed

columns.description: total_hours_worked / employment, for screening.
columns.name: hours_per_employee

columns.description: 0 where hours per employee falls outside 200-5,000. FLAGGED, NOT FIXED (10 of 485 rows). The implausible ones are real filings of something else - a construction project booking contractor hours against a casino establishment reported 19 employees and 117,335 hours.

columns.description: Names the script that CORRECTED this row's tribe attribution after it was merged. Set by 262 on 133 Form 5500 rows whose tribe came from 4wheeler's resolver and was wrong - a short place-derived spine name capturing an unrelated employer (the Native Village of Eagle, Alaska, on `Golden Eagle Casino` in Kansas), a token capture (`Prairie Band` on Prairie Meadows, Iowa), a same-name-different-tribe error (the Oklahoma Sac and Fox Nation on the Kansas tribe's casino), or a class violation (a BIE school on a casino).
